name: Enduvo
beats:
Expertise,
with a new address.
I redesigned Enduvo’s website: a new home for a platform built around human expertise.

A little movement.
A clearer story.
Scroll-led moments bring the product into focus, one idea at a time.

The whole thing
has to hang together.
Type, pacing, product, and the path through it all. I like working across the whole picture.

name: Embed3D
beats:
Go on.
Take it apart.
I designed and built Embed3D, a tool for creating interactive 3D lessons.

Some things make
more sense in 3D.
Turn the model. Slice into it. Find the part you need to understand.

And then,
put it anywhere.
Bring the lesson into a website or learning platform. A complicated object, made approachable.

name: Cerca
beats:
You know
a place.
The places I want to go tend to come from people whose taste I trust.

Now you know
where you put it.
Cerca gives those recommendations a home. Search the collection and open a place.

Taste is personal.
So is the map.
A place is more useful when you know who saved it. Explore my actual collection.

name: Illustrative
beats:
What if a book
could become a comic?
A question that became Illustrative: software for turning stories into illustrated books.

Page by page.
Panel by panel.
Characters, compositions, and words have to hold together across a whole story.

The output
is the fun part.
A finished book you can read, share, and export. An idea becomes something you can hold onto.

name: Murmur
beats:
My eyes would
like a break.
Murmur reads text aloud from the apps you’re already using.

A shortcut.
Then, a voice.
A small menu bar app, close at hand. Press ⌘⇧L and listen.

I like small
solutions.
Especially the kind that fit into an existing habit. This one lives quietly in the menu bar.

name: Tufte
beats:
A chart can
travel light.
Tufte makes portable charts for places where text already works.

Same rows.
Another way to see.
Change the chart, keep the data. Simple marks can carry a lot of meaning.

And you should
be able to check it.
Supporting evidence belongs with the chart. Clarity includes knowing where the numbers came from.

name: Dasha-FM
beats:
A little room
for reflection.
Dasha was an exploration of astrology and daily reflection.

Some projects
change direction.
The astrology app is now retired. That is part of its story, too.

Still curious.
Still making.
Today, the site points to Out Loud: one thoughtful question and a minute to answer it aloud. A smaller experiment in reflection.

name: Scroll Video Scrubber
beats:
Plot twist.
I made this part too.
The videos on this page move with a JavaScript plugin I built.

You scroll.
Time follows.
Forward, backward, or right to that one frame. The page stays in your hands.

A small tool.
A lot of possibilities.
Use it for your own idea. The source is open, and the scrolling is still just scrolling.
